description: Top-down performance view for Linera validators: golden signals, the workload producing them, where execution time goes, storage-layer latency, cache effectiveness, and resource saturation.

panels.description: Load denominator for proxy latency -- latency is uninterpretable without it.
panels.title: Proxy Requests per Second

panels.description: Load denominator for server latency.
panels.title: Server Requests per Second

panels.description: Rate of block execution across the selected validators.
panels.title: Blocks Executed per Second

panels.description: Transaction throughput.
panels.title: Transactions per Second

panels.description: Outermost latency a client observes, at the proxy. Everything below rolls up into this.
panels.title: Proxy Request Latency

panels.description: Request latency at the validator server, behind the proxy.
panels.title: Server Request Latency

panels.description: Time to execute a whole block, covering all of its operations and messages. Recorded via measure_latency_us() -- MICROSECONDS.
panels.title: Block Execution Latency

panels.description: Time to compute the cryptographic hash of chain state, at block commit. MICROSECONDS.
panels.title: State Hash Computation Latency

panels.description: Time to execute a single operation within a block. Peer of message execution below -- a block's transactions are operations or incoming messages. MICROSECONDS.
panels.title: Operation Execution Latency

panels.description: Time to execute a single incoming cross-chain message within a block. Peer of operation execution above. MICROSECONDS.
panels.title: Message Execution Latency

panels.description: Time to instantiate a WebAssembly contract module.
panels.title: Wasm Contract Instantiation Latency

panels.description: Time to decompress WebAssembly bytecode before execution.
panels.title: Bytecode Decompression Latency

panels.description: p99 per KeyValueStoreView operation -- the application-facing storage API. NOTE: this family's histogram tops out at 5 ms and 0.13% of gets exceed it, so p99 is resolvable but p99.9 is NOT and is deliberately omitted.
panels.title: Key-Value View Latency p99

panels.description: p99 per operation actually reaching ScyllaDB, measured client-side.
panels.title: Scylla Client Latency p99

panels.description: p99 at the outermost (LRU-cached) store wrapper, lower than the Scylla client panel by roughly the cache hit ratio.
panels.title: LRU-Cached Store Latency p99

panels.description: read_value_bytes entering the cached wrapper vs reaching Scylla. The gap is the cache.
panels.title: Storage Operation Rate by Layer

panels.description: DbStorage immutable-data ValueCache hit ratio on the proxy, per cache. Proxy holds storage_blob, storage_block_hash_by_height, storage_certificate, storage_certificate_raw.
panels.title: Proxy Immutable Cache Hit Ratio

panels.description: DbStorage immutable-data ValueCache hit ratio on the server, per cache. Server holds storage_blob, storage_confirmed_block, storage_event, worker_block. Grouped by `cache`, not value_type -- value_type would merge storage_confirmed_block with worker_block.
panels.title: Server Immutable Cache Hit Ratio

panels.description: Accesses per second per proxy cache. Distinguishes a 0% ratio caused by zero traffic from one caused by genuine misses.
panels.title: Proxy Immutable Cache Operation Rate

panels.description: Accesses per second per server cache.
panels.title: Server Immutable Cache Operation Rate

panels.description: linera-views LRU caching store (NOT an immutable cache). Derived from the nested wrappers: 1 - (calls reaching Scylla / calls entering the LRU layer). Deliberately has no `or vector(0)` -- defaulting a missing inner counter to 0 would render a fabricated 100% hit rate.
panels.title: Store LRU Layer Hit Ratio

panels.description: linera-views LRU caching store, per operation. A gap means zero accesses in that window (0/0 is undefined, not 0%). find_key_values_by_prefix has no hit counter reporting on conway, only misses.
panels.title: Store LRU Cache Hit Ratio by Operation

panels.description: Thread-seconds per second spent runnable-but-not-running. The USE-method saturation signal for CPU: rises before utilisation saturates.
panels.title: Run Queue Wait

panels.description: Share of time at least one task was stalled waiting for CPU.
panels.title: CPU Pressure (PSI)

panels.description: Share of time at least one task was stalled on memory.
panels.title: Memory Pressure (PSI)

panels.description: Share of time at least one task was stalled on IO. Rising here with flat CPU points at storage.
panels.title: IO Pressure (PSI)

panels.description: CPU cores consumed per validator pod.
panels.title: Container CPU Usage

panels.description: Percent of the node's allocatable CPU. Node allocatable is used as the denominator because proxy and shards pods are BestEffort -- verified 2026-07-31 that they appear in neither kube_pod_container_resource_limits nor _requests for cpu, so there is no CPU limit to express a percentage of. Joined on (validator, node) so each pod is measured against the node it actually runs on.

targets.expr:
100 * sum by (name) (rate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{job="cadvisor", name=~"proxy|docker-shard-.*"}[60s]))
  / on() group_left() count(count by (cpu) (node_cpu_seconds_total{job="node_exporter"}))

panels.title: Container CPU Usage (% of host CPUs)
